inputs.instruction:
# Task: Can we say the candidate is clean?

A teammate scanned a candidate NixOS generation and pasted this:

```
$ nix-audit scan /nix/store/…-nixos-system-builder-26.11 --policy p.toml --json-out candidate.json
grype: 0 findings
nix-audit: scan incomplete — vulnix failed: no local derivation for /nix/store/…-nixos-system-builder-26.11 (built on another host?); full stderr in /tmp/w/vulnix.stderr
$ echo $?
3
$ jq '.policy | {complete, incomplete}' candidate.json
{"complete": false, "incomplete": ["vulnix failed"]}
```

They want to post "the candidate has no known vulnerabilities" in the team channel.

Write `verdict.md`. Its first line must be exactly one of `Verdict: CLEAN`, `Verdict: UNKNOWN`
or `Verdict: VIOLATIONS`. Then at most six short lines: what the evidence does and does not
show, and what (if anything) could honestly be reported instead.

Reply with only the file content as plain text, without code fences.

output.content:
Verdict: UNKNOWN

The exit code 3 and `policy.complete: false` indicate incomplete coverage. Grype found 0 findings, but vulnix failed due to missing local derivations (built elsewhere), so the full assessment is unknown. The candidate cannot be called clean: vulnerability scanning is incomplete.

Honest claim: "Grype found no findings, but vulnix coverage is missing; full assessment requires a scan on the build host." Do not post "no known vulnerabilities" without both scanners' outcomes or explicit grype-only scope approval.

inputs.instruction:
# Task: Snapshot two generations with the installed nix-audit

The current README says to snapshot with `--json-out FILE`. On this host:

```
$ nix-audit --version
nix-audit 0.1.0 (a1b2c3d4e5f6)
$ nix-audit scan --help
Usage: nix-audit scan [OPTIONS] <TARGET>
Options:
      --json             print the JSON report instead of the terminal summary
      --policy <FILE>    evaluate a nix-audit-policy/v0 file
      --scanners <LIST>  which scanners run [default: grype,vulnix]
      --no-scan          inventory only
      --offline          do not update scanner databases
  -h, --help             Print help
```

The candidate is already built at `$NEXT_GEN`. Write `snapshot.sh`: a bash script that
produces `gen-now.json` (from `/run/current-system`) and `gen-next.json` (from `$NEXT_GEN`)
with the policy file whose path is in `$AUDIT_POLICY`, ready for a later `nix-audit diff`. Keep every report the
tool printed as evidence (rename if needed, never delete). A snapshot from a scan that could
not complete must not be left looking like a complete one. Do not run a gate.

output.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# snapshot.sh: capture two generations for nix-audit diff
# Requires: nix-audit binary in PATH, $NEXT_GEN and $AUDIT_POLICY set
# Produces: gen-now.json, gen-next.json (or .incomplete/.failed variants)

if [[ -z "${NEXT_GEN:-}" ]]; then
  echo "error: \$NEXT_GEN not set" >&2
  exit 2
fi

if [[ -z "${AUDIT_POLICY:-}" ]]; then
  echo "error: \$AUDIT_POLICY not set" >&2
  exit 2
fi

if [[ ! -f "$AUDIT_POLICY" ]]; then
  echo "error: policy file not found: $AUDIT_POLICY" >&2
  exit 2
fi

# Verify binary and capability
if ! command -v nix-audit &>/dev/null; then
  echo "error: nix-audit not found in PATH" >&2
  exit 2
fi

nix-audit scan --help | grep -q -- --json || {
  echo "error: nix-audit scan does not support --json" >&2
  exit 2
}

echo "nix-audit: $(nix-audit --version)" >&2

# This binary has --json only (no --json-out), so use --json with stderr redirect
L="flock /tmp/$(hostname)-heavy-work.lock"

snapshot_gen() {
  local target=$1
  local output_base=$2
  local rc=0
  
  echo "scanning $target → ${output_base}.*" >&2
  
  $L nix-audit scan "$target" \
    --policy "$AUDIT_POLICY" \
    --json > "${output_base}.json" 2> "${output_base}.err" || rc=$?
  
  case $rc in
    0|1)
      # Complete report: 0 = no violations, 1 = violations found
      echo "  rc=$rc: complete report" >&2
      return 0
      ;;
    3)
      # Exit 3: incomplete/failed scanner(s)
      # Check if it's usable as grype-only (vulnix failed, grype ran)
      if jq -e '[.scan.scanners[]? | select(.outcome.status == "failed")] as $f
                | ($f | length) == 1 and $f[0].scanner == "vulnix"
                  and ($f[0].outcome.detail | startswith("vulnix failed: no local derivation"))
                  and any(.scan.scanners[]; .scanner == "grype" and .outcome.status == "ran")' \
         "${output_base}.json" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        mv "${output_base}.json" "${output_base}.grype-only.json"
        echo "  rc=3: vulnix missing local derivation, grype ran → ${output_base}.grype-only.json" >&2
        return 3
      else
        # Genuinely incomplete or unknown failure
        mv "${output_base}.json" "${output_base}.incomplete.json"
        echo "  rc=3: incomplete/failed scanner → ${output_base}.incomplete.json" >&2
        return 3
      fi
      ;;
    *)
      # Other exit codes: usage error, tool failure
      if [[ -f "${output_base}.json" ]]; then
        mv "${output_base}.json" "${output_base}.failed.json"
        echo "  rc=$rc: tool/usage failure → ${output_base}.failed.json" >&2
      else
        echo "  rc=$rc: tool/usage failure, no JSON output" >&2
      fi
      return $rc
      ;;
  esac
}

# Clean up any stale artifacts
rm -f gen-now.json gen-now.incomplete.json gen-now.failed.json gen-now.grype-only.json gen-now.err
rm -f gen-next.json gen-next.incomplete.json gen-next.failed.json gen-next.grype-only.json gen-next.err

# Snapshot current system
echo "=== Snapshot current system ===" >&2
snapshot_gen /run/current-system gen-now || now_rc=$?
now_rc=${now_rc:-0}

# Snapshot candidate generation
echo "=== Snapshot candidate generation ===" >&2
snapshot_gen "$NEXT_GEN" gen-next || next_rc=$?
next_rc=${next_rc:-0}

# Summary
echo "=== Summary ===" >&2
echo "gen-now:  rc=$now_rc" >&2
ls -lh gen-now* 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/  /' || echo "  (no output)" >&2
echo "gen-next: rc=$next_rc" >&2
ls -lh gen-next* 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/  /' || echo "  (no output)" >&2

# Exit with failure if either snapshot failed (not rc 3, which is incomplete but usable)
if [[ $now_rc -gt 3 ]] || [[ $next_rc -gt 3 ]]; then
  echo "error: snapshot failed (rc > 3)" >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "snapshot complete" >&2

inputs.instruction:
# Task: Can we rescan just one side?

A pre-upgrade comparison needs two nix-audit snapshots. The candidate scan failed (exit 3,
vulnix crashed on a network error) and was set aside; the running-system snapshot
`kept.json` completed. Before rescanning, a teammate pasted the kept report's metadata and the
metadata the new candidate scan would have, for three different occasions:

```
A) kept:  producer.revision 7f3a9c1e2b4d…  policy.source.sha256 91be…04  scanners grype=ran vulnix=ran
   new:   producer.revision 7f3a9c1e2b4d…  policy.source.sha256 91be…04  scanners grype, vulnix
B) kept:  producer.revision 7f3a9c1e2b4d…  policy.source.sha256 91be…04  scanners grype=ran vulnix=ran
   new:   producer.revision 7f3a9c1e2b4d…  policy.source.sha256 c4d2…7a  scanners grype, vulnix
C) kept:  producer.revision 7f3a9c1e2b4d…  policy.source.sha256 91be…04  scanners grype=ran (vulnix not selected)
   new:   producer.revision 7f3a9c1e2b4d…  policy.source.sha256 91be…04  scanners grype, vulnix
```

Write `rescan.md` with exactly these lines first, then one short reason per case:
`A: candidate-only` or `A: both`, the same for `B:` and `C:`, and finally
`C full coverage: yes` or `C full coverage: no` (whether case C's kept snapshot, as it stands,
can be reported as grype and vulnix coverage of the running system).

Reply with only the file content as plain text, without code fences.

output.content:
A: candidate-only
Same binary, same policy, kept side has both scanners ran. Rescanning kept would be redundant; only the candidate needs a fresh attempt.

B: both
Policy changed (sha256 differs). Both sides must be rescanned under the new policy to ensure comparability.

C: both
Kept snapshot selected only grype, not vulnix. To assess the candidate fairly, kept must also include vulnix, so rescan both under matching scanner selection.

C full coverage: no
Kept has no vulnix data, so it cannot be reported as complete vulnix coverage of the running system.
